title: Android Dedicated (COSU) / Kiosk Device Enrollment & Management in Intune
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Microsoft Android implementation).

Intune admin center / Microsoft Graph / managed Google Play / Google Admin console authored at exact detail from Microsoft & Google public docs. The Android Management API (AMAPI) transition, web/account-driven enrollment, and whether a change triggers device RE-ENROLLMENT are actively evolving — cited or flagged 'verify against current Microsoft guidance / your tenant', never asserted from memory or invented. OEM (Samsung Knox/Zebra) + third-party apps at the pattern level. Automation is PowerShell (Graph); no hardcoded credentials/secrets. No client names.
hook: Deploy locked-down Android dedicated/kiosk devices at scale
problem: Frontline, warehouse, retail, and clinical dedicated Android devices need to boot straight into one app or a curated set — no personal use, no wandering. This solution stands up Android dedicated (COSU) devices in Intune: enrollment via token / QR / NFC / zero-touch, the kiosk profile (single-app or multi-app), device restrictions, managed Google Play app delivery, and remote management — so a fleet of purpose-built devices deploys consistently and stays locked down.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the dedicated/COSU model, enrollment methods (token/QR/NFC/zero-touch), single- vs multi-app kiosk, and the OEM/rugged considerations at pattern level.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (Intune + Android Enterprise + managed Google Play, admin roles, device hardware, network).

Implementation Guide — create the dedicated enrollment profile, build the kiosk (single/multi-app) + restrictions, assign managed Google Play apps, enroll via the chosen method, and validate the locked-down experience — pilot-first, each profile named.

5 PowerShell scripts — Discovery, Configuration/Remediation, Validation, Reporting, and a scope/health helper — authentic Microsoft Graph / Intune automation (read-only or -WhatIf by default; no credentials in code).
Validation gates (devices boot to kiosk, only allowed apps, remote-manageable) plus Best Practices for a scalable dedicated-device fleet.
short: Stand up Android dedicated (COSU) / kiosk devices in Intune — token/QR/NFC/zero-touch enrollment, single/multi-app kiosk, restrictions, managed Google Play apps, and remote management — so purpose-built devices deploy consistently and stay locked down. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
